welcome:
Welcome! Whether you want to put on a fresh new skin, share your pixel-art creations with the community, or join your friends' server using external authentication, this guide will walk you through every step.

Before diving in, take a quick moment to understand two key concepts: your **account** is your master key that stores your profile, settings, and collected textures; while your **character** is your actual identity inside the Minecraft world. Each character has its own unique name and can wear its own skin and cape.

## First time here?

If you are new around here, follow our [Newbie Guide](/manual/quick-start) step by step: sign up an account → create your first in-game character → pick and apply your favorite textures → configure your game client. You'll be ready to show off your new look in minutes!

If you have already dressed up your character on the website and just want to get it working in the game, jump straight to the [CustomSkinLoader setup](/manual/customskinloader) or the [External Login guide](/manual/yggdrasil).

> **Helpful reminder**: Your website username, texture titles, and in-game character names are completely independent. When Minecraft loads your skin, it always looks for the exact character name you created under "Character Management".

## Find what you need

- **Customize your look**: Browse or [Upload Textures](/manual/textures), and mix & match in [My Wardrobe](/manual/closet).
- **Manage your account**: Check [Account & Email](/manual/account) security, and manage launcher permissions under [Application Authorization](/manual/applications).
- **Community guidelines**: Learn how [Points & Check-in](/manual/score) keep things running smoothly, and help protect creators under [Creations & Reporting](/manual/copyright).
- **Running into trouble?**: Check out solutions to common pitfalls in the [FAQ](/manual/faq), or reach out to us using the tips in [Ask for Help](/manual/help).

## Site features and rules

Every skin server is independently hosted and maintained by its own administration team. Registration methods, maximum character limits, upload size restrictions, and daily check-in rewards are configured based on the site's specific policies.

Keep in mind that Minecraft versions, mod loaders (such as Forge, Fabric, or NeoForge), and launchers all have small differences. Before dropping mods or configuration files into your game, double-check that the files match your current client instance.
quick-start:
Ready to leave the default Steve and Alex look behind and step into the blocky world with your own style? Getting set up is quick and easy—just follow these four simple steps.

## 1. Prepare your account

First, head over to the [Registration page](/register) to create your personal account. If you already have one, simply [Log in](/login). If third-party login is enabled on the site, you can also sign in with one click.

If this is your first time logging in through a third party, follow the on-screen prompts to complete any missing profile details. Then visit your [User Center](/user) to verify your email. Clicking the confirmation link sent to your inbox makes recovering your account much easier down the road.

## 2. Create a character

Once logged in, open [Character Management](/player), click "Add Character", and enter the player name you plan to use in the game.

This step is crucial: if you play in offline mode or use a skin mod like CustomSkinLoader, the character name here must match your launcher's in-game name letter for letter (including uppercase and lowercase). If you use external authentication, you will be able to select this character right inside your launcher. Learn more in [Creating and Managing Characters](/manual/players).

## 3. Set up your skin and cape

With a character ready, it's time to dress it up! Browse the [Skin Library](/skinlib) for a skin or cape you love, open its details page, and click "Apply to character". You can also save it to your wardrobe first so you can switch back whenever you like.

If you already have a custom skin PNG file on your computer, head to [Upload Texture](/skinlib/upload), upload your file, double-check the 3D preview, and apply it to your character.

> **Don't miss this step**: Collecting a skin or uploading a PNG only stores it in your wardrobe. You must actively **apply** it to your character on the details page or in Character Management, otherwise your character will still show up with the default look in-game.

## 4. Configure your game

Now that your character is dressed, the final step is telling your Minecraft client where to fetch your textures. Choose the guide that matches your setup:

| Usage Scenario | Reading Guide |
| --- | --- |
| Use skin Mod to load the texture of this site | [Configuration CustomSkinLoader](/manual/customskinloader) |
| The server requires account authentication for this site | [Yggdrasil External login ](/manual/yggdrasil) |

Once configured, launch your game and enjoy your new look! If you still see the default skin, don't worry—open our [FAQ](/manual/faq) to verify your character name spelling, texture application status, and mod folders.
account:
Your account is your home on this skin site. Taking good care of it ensures your carefully assembled characters and favorite textures stay safe.

Your email address is your primary safeguard for receiving security notices and recovering your password. We strongly recommend linking a private mailbox that you can reliably access long-term.

## Registration and login

You can join anytime through the [Registration](/register) page, or log in via third-party providers if supported. If registration appears closed or restricted, the administrators may be performing routine maintenance or limiting new sign-ups; feel free to contact them for details.

When signing in via a third party for the first time, the site will guide you through setting up an email, display name, or an independent site password. Completing these quick steps unlocks the full power of character management and the wardrobe.

## Verify your email

Verifying your email prevents accidental account loss and unlocks key community features:

1. Log in and go to your [User Center](/user) or [Personal Information](/profile).
2. Confirm that your email address is correct, then click to send a verification email.
3. Check your inbox and click the verification link in the email.
4. Return to the site and refresh the page to see your verified status.

If the email doesn't arrive right away, don't panic—check your spam or junk folder, and make sure there are no typos in the address. If you need to resend, please wait for the countdown timer to finish. Expired links can be re-requested easily on the site, so avoid clicking old emails repeatedly.

## Reset and update password

If you ever forget your password, there's no need to stress. Open [Retrieve Password](/forgot-password), enter your registered email, and follow the instructions in the reset email. If you are already logged in, you can update your password anytime in [Personal Information](/profile).

If you initially registered through a third-party service without creating an independent password, we highly recommend adding one in your profile settings. This allows you to log in smoothly to traditional launchers and third-party tools that require password authentication.

## Protect your account

Your password, email verification links, login tokens, and device codes are strictly confidential. Never share screenshots of them with others or type them into unverified third-party websites.

Always remember to log out when using shared computers in libraries, schools, or internet cafes. If you suspect any unauthorized activity, change your password immediately and visit [Application Authorization](/user/applications) to inspect and revoke any unfamiliar connections.
players:
Characters represent your presence in the Minecraft world. In the skin system, each character has its own name and can independently equip one skin and one cape. You can style different characters to match different servers, moods, or roleplay themes.

## Create a character

1. Open [Character Management](/player).
2. Click "Add Character" and type in the name you want to use in the game.
3. Review the naming guidelines shown on the screen and submit.

Name length rules, allowed character sets, character limits per user, and creation costs depend on the server's settings. If your preferred name is already taken, try a creative variation or suffix. If validation fails, adjust the spelling as suggested on the page.

> **Important note**: Your website account display name is not your in-game character name. If you use a skin mod, the player name you enter into your game launcher must match this character name **exactly** (including capitalization) for textures to load properly.

## Set skin and cape

Click on a character in your list to view its current look on the right. Switch between the "Skin" and "Cape" tabs to browse your wardrobe and equip textures. Skins and capes are completely independent—equipping a new cape will never overwrite your existing skin.

If a texture you want doesn't show up in your list, make sure it has already been added to [My Wardrobe](/closet) and that its type matches what you are equipping. You can also apply textures directly to your active character from any texture's detail page in the skin library.

![Character management: After selecting the character, switch the skin or cloak on the right and select the texture](/manual/players.jpg)

## Rename and delete

As your adventures evolve, you may want to refresh a character's name or clean up retired profiles. You can rename or delete characters at any time from the character management page.

Keep in mind: after renaming a character, remember to update the in-game name in your launcher if you use offline mode or skin mods. If you use external authentication, simply refresh your account in the launcher to pull the latest character list.

Think carefully before deleting a character. Point refunds upon deletion depend on site rules; more importantly, multiplayer servers usually track inventories, claims, and player data by character name or UUID. Check with your server administrator beforehand if you are unsure about preserving your game progress.
textures:
The Skin Library is a creative hub where our community shares and discovers styles. Here, you can browse a wide collection of public skins and capes, or upload your own original PNG textures.

## Use textures from the skin library

Head over to the [Skin Library](/skinlib) to filter by skins or capes, or search for specific styles with keywords. Click any card to open its detail page and spin the interactive 3D model to inspect every angle. From there, you can save the texture to your wardrobe or apply it directly to your in-game character.

Please show respect for original creators. While public textures are free to enjoy and wear in-game, that does not give anyone permission to re-upload them without credit or use them for commercial distribution.

![Skin Library: Search for works and filter by texture type](/manual/skinlib.jpg)

When you click "Apply to character" on the detail page, a dialog will ask which character should receive the new look. If you have several characters, make sure you choose the right one before confirming.

![Texture details: Preview the skin and view download, collection and application entrance](/manual/texture-detail.jpg)

![Apply to Character: Select the character whose texture you want to change the texture from the list](/manual/apply-texture.jpg)

## Upload a PNG

If you created your own skin or have a favorite texture saved on your computer, uploading it is straightforward:

1. Visit [Upload Texture](/skinlib/upload), then click to select your PNG file or drag and drop it into the upload box.
2. Give your creation a name, and select whether it is a "Skin" or a "Cape".
3. When uploading a skin, this setting is critical: pick the correct model type—Classic (Steve) or Slim (Alex).
4. Choose whether to make it public or private, review the 3D preview and point cost, and hit submit.
5. Once uploaded, click "Apply to character" on the detail page to put on your new texture!

Why does model type matter so much? Classic models (Steve) feature 4-pixel wide arms, while Slim models (Alex) have 3-pixel wide arms. Choosing the wrong model can result in unsightly black seams or distorted arm textures in-game.

![Upload texture: Select PNG, fill in name, type, model and visibility ](/manual/upload.jpg)

> **Helpful tip**: Minecraft skins require a specific unfolded UV texture layout. Simply renaming a photo, avatar, or screenshot to end in `.png` will not work; attempting to upload non-skin images will only look scrambled and broken on your character.

## Public vs. private

Marking a texture as "Public" showcases it in the public library where other players can admire, collect, and rate your work. If a skin is a private commission for you and your friends, or you just want to keep it personal, set it to "Private"—it will stay hidden from the public catalog.

Keep in mind that "Private" does not mean end-to-end encrypted storage; Minecraft clients still need to fetch the image file to render your character in the world, so never upload files containing real-life personal privacy or sensitive information. Toggling visibility may involve small point adjustments as indicated on the screen.

## Edit and delete

On the detail page of any texture you own, you can update its title, edit its description, adjust its visibility, or correct its model type. After making changes, rotate the 3D preview to make sure everything looks pristine.

If you no longer need a texture, you can delete it. Before doing so, check whether any of your characters are currently wearing it so you don't leave them empty-handed. Point refunds and upload reward adjustments follow standard server rules.
closet:
Your wardrobe is your personal dressing room on the skin server. Whenever you spot a neat design in the library or upload a creation of your own, you can store it here to easily switch styles whenever you want.

Newcomers often wonder: "Why did I add a skin to my wardrobe, but my character in the game hasn't changed?" Think of it just like buying clothes in real life—hanging a new outfit in your closet doesn't mean you're wearing it yet. You still have to pick it out and put it on your character!

## Save textures to closet

While browsing the [Skin Library](/skinlib), whenever you find something you like, open its detail page and click "Add to Wardrobe". Your own newly uploaded textures are also automatically tucked into your wardrobe for convenience.

Depending on the site's setup, saving a texture may cost a tiny point maintenance fee as shown on the screen. If you already have that texture in your wardrobe, there is no need to add it again.

## Organize and wear

Whenever you feel like changing your style, open [My Wardrobe](/closet) to see all your saved skins and capes in one place. You can even assign custom nicknames to your saved items—these notes are purely for your own reference to make sorting easy, and won't alter the creator's original title.

Once you've settled on the perfect match, click to apply it to your character right from the wardrobe card, or head to [Character Management](/player) to fine-tune your outfit.

![My Wardrobe: Collect textures and apply to characters, rename and remove entries](/manual/closet.jpg)

## Remove from closet

If your wardrobe is getting cluttered with old outfits you've moved on from, click "Remove from wardrobe" to take them off your personal list. Rest assured: removing an item from your wardrobe only clears it from your private collection; it will never delete the creator's original upload in the skin library or affect other players who love wearing it.

If a saved texture ever turns into an unavailable placeholder, it usually means the original work was deleted by the author, switched to private, or removed by moderators. When that happens, simply browse the library for a fresh new look.
customskinloader:
CustomSkinLoader (commonly known as CSL, or the Universal Skin Mod) is one of the most widely used client-side skin mods in the Minecraft community. Once installed, it automatically fetches your customized skins and capes from this site based on your in-game player name—even in standard offline mode.

## Getting ready before installation

Before diving into configuration, take a minute to check two small prerequisites:
1. Head over to [Character Management](/player) to make sure you have created a character whose name matches your launcher's offline player name exactly (including uppercase/lowercase letters), and that you have applied a skin or cape to it.
2. Confirm your Minecraft version and mod loader (such as Forge, Fabric, or NeoForge), then visit the [CustomSkinLoader official release page ](https://github.com/xfl03/MCCustomSkinLoader/releases) to download the matching mod file.

Place the downloaded `.jar` file directly into your game instance's `mods` folder. If you use version isolation in your launcher (where each game version has its own separate folder), be sure to open the folder for the specific instance you are playing.

## Download the site configuration

Once the mod is in place, you need to point CSL toward this skin server:

1. Launch your game with CSL installed once, reach the main menu, and then quit. This allows CSL to generate its local configuration folder structure automatically.
2. Open our [Configuration Generator](/user/config) page.
3. Download the custom "ExtraList" configuration file.
4. Place that downloaded file into your instance's `.minecraft/CustomSkinLoader/ExtraList` folder.
5. Launch the game again. As long as your player name matches your character name on this site, your custom skin will load onto your character!

![Configuration generation: Download ExtraList on the left, view CSL and Universal Skin Mod on the right to configure ](/manual/customskinloader.jpg)

**Here is a very common question**: After your first successful launch, you might notice that the file you placed in the `ExtraList` folder has suddenly disappeared. Don't worry! It wasn't lost or deleted; CSL intelligently merges ExtraList entries into its main configuration file after reading them. This is completely normal behavior, and you do not need to download it again.

> **Helpful reminder**: `ExtraList` is a folder. Keep the downloaded file in its original JSON format. Do not unzip it, rename it to plain text, or drop it into the `mods` folder by mistake.

## Manual configuration and loading order

If you prefer manual tweaks, our configuration generator also displays the raw JSON snippet for you to paste into CSL's `CustomSkinLoader.json` file. Before editing manually, make a quick backup of your config file, ensure valid JSON formatting, and verify that the API URLs in the `loadlist` are intact.

Why does the order in `loadlist` matter? If your in-game name happens to match an official Mojang Minecraft account, the loading order determines who takes precedence—this skin site or Mojang? Using our generator ensures this site is placed at the top of the priority list.

## Other mods

If you use UniSkinMod instead of CSL, you can also grab the appropriate config snippet from the [Configuration Generator ](/user/config). Config formats differ between mods, so avoid mixing CSL files with other mods.

If your skin still isn't loading in-game, don't get discouraged! Most of the time it's just a misplaced folder or a minor typo. Check your mod list to verify CSL is active, then follow our [In-game loading troubleshooting](/manual/faq#section-3) step by step.
yggdrasil:
Yggdrasil external authentication is an elegant and reliable way to connect to compatible servers. If your game launcher supports the authlib-injector protocol, you can log into your launcher directly using your site account credentials. Your in-game identity and custom skins will load automatically, without needing any client-side skin mods.

> **Please note**: External login provides independent authentication for community servers. It is not a replacement for an official Mojang/Microsoft Minecraft license, and it will not allow you to join servers that only accept official Microsoft authentication.

## Prepare account and role

Before setting up your launcher, make sure your basics are in order:
Finish your [Email and Account Settings](/manual/account), create at least one [Character](/manual/players) on the site, and equip your preferred skin or cape.

If you usually sign in through third-party services and haven't created an independent site password yet, visit [Personal Information](/profile) to set one up. If your launcher supports web authorization, you can also follow its prompts to authenticate directly through your browser.

## Add authentication server

This site's Yggdrasil API authentication address is:

`{{site_url}}/api/yggdrasil`

In popular launchers that support external login (such as HMCL, PCL2, or Prism Launcher), open Account Settings, choose "Add Account" → "External Login / Auth Server (authlib-injector)", and paste the full address above.

To make things even easier, the launcher configuration widget in your [User Center](/user) lets you copy the URL with one click, or even drag and drop the card directly into supported launcher windows to auto-configure.

## Log in and select a role

1. Select the authentication server you just added in your launcher.
2. Enter your registered email address and site password.
3. After authentication succeeds, the launcher will fetch all characters under your account. Pick the one you want to play with and launch the game!

A quick safety reminder: this login form communicates with this skin server, so enter your password for this site—never enter your official Microsoft password here. If your character list appears empty after logging in, simply return to Character Management on the site, create a character, and hit refresh in your launcher.

## Join multiplayer server

If you plan to join a friend's or community multiplayer server, check with the server owner first to verify that their server connects to this site's authentication backend. A seamless multiplayer experience requires matching authentication sources on both the client and server.

Server administrators looking to set up external auth can consult the [Official Project Description ](https://github.com/yushijinhun/authlib-injector) to attach authlib-injector to the server startup flags pointing to this site. Avoid setting `online-mode=false` just to bypass errors; keeping external auth active protects your server from bot attacks while ensuring everyone's skins look great.

## Web and device authorization

Some modern third-party launchers and utility tools offer an even smoother login experience: they may redirect your browser to an authorization confirmation page, or provide a short device code for you to enter on our [Device Authorization Page](/connect/device). When prompted, review the application name and requested permissions, and approve only if you initiated the request.

You can review all granted permissions anytime under [Application Authorization](/user/applications) and revoke old devices with one click. For deeper details, check out the [Application Authorization Manual](/manual/applications).
premium:
If this site has enabled official Minecraft account verification, you can link your genuine Minecraft Java Edition profile with your account here. This protects your in-game name and often earns you bonus points as a token of appreciation.

## Start verification

Log in and visit your [User Center](/user), locate the account verification section, and click the verification button. You will be securely directed to Microsoft's official sign-in portal. Simply log into the Microsoft account that owns your Minecraft Java Edition license and authorize access; once complete, you will be redirected back to see your verified badge.

Whether this feature is active and how many reward points are granted depends on server policy. If you don't see the verification card in your User Center, the feature may be temporarily disabled; feel free to ask an administrator for details.

## View and unbind

Once verified, you can check your linked character name and status under [Personal Information](/profile). If you ever change your official Minecraft username with Mojang, simply click the verification button again to refresh your linked identity.

If you ever need to unlink your profile, review the confirmation prompt carefully. Your official account link, site-created characters, and third-party login bindings are managed independently; when disconnecting one, make sure you still have at least one working login method to access your account.

## When verification fails

If verification runs into a hitch, confirm that the Microsoft account you logged into actually owns a Minecraft Java Edition license (not Bedrock-only or trial edition) and that you have launched the game to establish an official in-game name. If you accidentally canceled the prompt or encountered a network timeout, make note of any error text and try again in a moment.

**One final reminder**: Linking an official Minecraft account on the site does not automatically replace your client's skin mod configuration, nor does it change server authentication rules. To display your custom skins in-game, you still need to set up your client following our [Client Configuration](/manual/customskinloader) or [External Login Guide](/manual/yggdrasil).
score:
Points are a helpful community mechanism used to maintain smooth server operations and balance storage costs. Whether you are checking in daily or uploading fantastic creations, points help keep the community thriving. Reward rates and fees vary between servers, so refer to the numbers shown on your site.

## View points and fees

Curious about your points balance? Visit your [User Center](/user) and click on your points card to expand a detailed breakdown. Here, you can review the reward for daily check-ins as well as the costs for creating characters, uploading textures, and saving items to your wardrobe.

Public and private textures may carry different upload rates. The upload page automatically calculates the required points based on your file size and chosen visibility, so take a quick glance at your balance before submitting.

## Check-in and rewards

Make it a habit to stop by and say hello! Head to your User Center and click the "Check In" button to claim your daily points reward. The page will also let you know when your next check-in becomes available. If the button is grayed out, check the timer or status message on the screen and check back when it resets.

In addition to daily check-ins, many servers offer welcome bonuses for new registrations, first-time texture uploads, or official account verification. These bonuses are configured by the administration team, so repeated attempts on inactive rewards will not yield extra points.

## Insufficient points

If an alert pops up saying you don't have enough points to create a character, upload a skin, or save to your wardrobe, don't worry! Check the exact fee required, and either check in again tomorrow or join community activities to earn more points.

To keep server storage healthy, some sites may charge a modest ongoing storage fee based on your total uploaded textures. Your User Center will display clear usage statistics and deduction rules. Optimizing texture dimensions before uploading and retiring unused textures helps keep your wardrobe lean and efficient.

## Deletions and refunds

Points handling when deleting characters, removing wardrobe items, or deleting textures varies by action. Some actions may refund a portion of previously spent points, while promotional bonus points may be reclaimed upon deletion. All specifics follow the server's published rules and confirmation prompts.
applications:
Application authorization lets trusted launchers and third-party tools interact with your account within strict boundaries you approve—all without ever exposing your account password. Before confirming an authorization request, always verify that you initiated the action yourself.

## Web page authorization

When a launcher or app opens your browser to our authorization page, the screen will clearly display the application's name, developer details, and the specific permissions it requests (such as viewing your character list).

Take a quick second to verify: is this the software you were just using? Are the requested permissions reasonable? If you don't recognize the app, if the prompt appeared out of nowhere, or if it asks for more access than necessary, you can safely cancel. Never forward the redirect URL or access token to anyone else.

## Device code authorization

On consoles, lightweight launchers, or terminal tools that cannot automatically open a web browser, the app may display a short device code instead:

1. Start the login process in your launcher to generate a device code on your screen.
2. Open the [Device Authorization Page](/connect/device) in your browser on your computer or phone.
3. Enter the exact code shown on your launcher screen.
4. Review the application name and permissions carefully, then confirm authorization to finish logging in.

If the code expires because too much time passed, simply generate a fresh code in your launcher. A critical security warning: never type in a mysterious device code sent by a stranger in a chat, as doing so grants their device access to your account.

## Revoke authorization

Over time, you might stop using older launchers or uninstall apps. You can inspect all currently authorized applications anytime under [Application Authorization](/user/applications).

If you see an app you no longer use or don't remember authorizing, click "Revoke" to instantly cancel its access token. Next time that software tries to connect, it will have to ask for your permission again.

## Your own applications

The "My Applications" tab on this page provides developer tools for managing OAuth clients. If you are an everyday Minecraft player, you simply need to approve prompts when using your favorite launcher—you don't need to create an application yourself.

If you are a developer building a custom launcher for your community or server, you can register your app here and configure callback URLs and permission scopes. Treat your Client Secret and user tokens with care—never hardcode or commit them to public repositories.
copyright:
Every great skin and cape represents hours of dedication and pixel-perfect creativity from its creator. Before sharing any work in our community, please ensure you have the rightful authority to upload and publish it. Being able to download a file from the web or see it in-game does not give anyone the right to claim ownership or republish it freely.

## Share your work

When uploading a skin or cape you designed entirely from scratch, feel free to share your inspiration, creative process, and any usage guidelines in the description so fellow players can appreciate your work.

If your creation is an adaptation, recolor, or remix of someone else's work, please verify beforehand that the original author allows remixes and reposts, and credit the original creator prominently with a link to their original post. Let's work together to respect creative effort and avoid removing watermark signatures.

## Report texture or comment

A welcoming community depends on everyone's vigilance. If you come across plagiarized content, copyright infringement, inappropriate imagery, or abusive comments in the library or comment sections, click the report button on the page right away.

When submitting a report, be concise, clear, and objective. If reporting copyright infringement, providing links to the original artist's earliest post or creation timeline will help moderators resolve the issue quickly. Avoid spamming duplicate reports or including unrelated personal details.

## Follow up

After submitting a report, check [My Report](/reports) anytime to track its review progress and read moderator responses. The moderation team reviews submissions fairly according to community guidelines; since investigating takes time, submitting a report does not mean an item will be instantly taken down.

If moderators need more context, you can provide further verifiable evidence in the report ticket. For complex copyright disputes, you can also reach out to the site administration as outlined in [Ask for help](/manual/help).
faq:
Experiencing issues with your skin not showing up, getting an unexpected error prompt, or feeling stuck? Take a deep breath! Identify whether the problem is occurring on the website, in your launcher, or inside the game world, and follow the matching checklist below.

## Account and Email

**Can't receive verification or password reset emails?**
First, check your spam, junk, or promotional folders, as email providers sometimes filter automated system messages. Make sure your email address was entered without typos or stray spaces. If you still haven't received it, wait for the on-screen countdown timer to expire before resending, rather than clicking repeatedly. If the problem persists, contact a site administrator to check the email delivery service.

**Why am I asked to complete profile details after third-party login?**
This helps establish a secure local profile on this site. Adding an email lets you recover your account if your third-party provider is ever inaccessible, and setting an independent password lets you log into traditional launchers that don't support browser popups.

**Can't find a specific button or feature?**
Certain site features (such as open registration, third-party linking, official account verification, or specific texture uploads) are enabled dynamically by administrators. Ensure you are logged in and have finished basic profile initialization; if it's still missing, ask your server admin about feature availability.

## Textures and Characters

**Why hasn't my skin updated in-game after adding it to my wardrobe?**
This is the most common pitfall for new players! Your wardrobe is simply your closet. Having clothes in your closet doesn't mean you are wearing them. Open Character Management, select your character, and click "Apply" on that texture to actually equip it.

**Why does uploading a texture fail?**
Verify that your file is an authentic PNG image (not just a JPEG or photo renamed to `.png`), and that its dimensions match Minecraft skin standards. Also check that your point balance covers any upload fees. If the error continues, note down the exact error message text for easier troubleshooting.

**Why are there black borders or transparent gaps around my character's arms?**
This happens when there is a mismatch between Classic models (Steve, 4-pixel arms) and Slim models (Alex, 3-pixel arms). Return to your texture's detail page, switch the model type to the correct one, and re-apply it to your character.

**My desired character name is already taken. What should I do?**
Character names are unique across the site. If your favorite name is taken, try an inventive variation or prefix/suffix. If the name belongs to an official Minecraft account you legally own, check whether the site offers official account verification to claim and protect matching names.

## In-game loading

If your 3D preview looks great on the website but your character still appears with a default skin in-game, run through this golden troubleshooting checklist:

1. **Check name spelling**: Does your launcher's in-game player name match your character name on this site **exactly**? (Capitalization, underscores, and letters must match identically—do not confuse this with your website username!)
2. **Confirm equipped status**: Verify on the site that the character has actively equipped the skin or cape.
3. **Verify mod files**: If using CustomSkinLoader, ensure you downloaded the build matching your Minecraft version and mod loader (Forge/Fabric), and that it is placed in the `mods` folder of the specific instance you are running.
4. **Check config placement**: Make sure the downloaded ExtraList file was placed in your instance's `.minecraft/CustomSkinLoader/ExtraList` directory. If you edited configs by hand, check for valid JSON syntax and correct URLs.
5. **Network and caching**: Skin changes sometimes take a moment to reflect due to network latency or local caches. Try exiting your world and re-entering, or restart your game client completely.

**Why can I see my custom skin, but my friends only see default Steve?**
Client-side skin mods like CustomSkinLoader only render custom textures for clients that also have the mod installed and properly configured. If your friends are running a vanilla unmodded client, they won't see your site skin. To share appearances with everyone, either have your friends install the mod configuration too, or have the server owner configure external Yggdrasil authentication.

## External login

**Password is correct, but the launcher says login failed?**
First, check that your launcher's auth server URL is set to this site's complete Yggdrasil API address. Next, make sure you are entering your site email and your **website password** (never enter your Microsoft password here). If your account was newly registered, make sure your email verification was completed.

**External login succeeded, but the launcher character list is empty?**
External authentication reads characters created in your account on this site. Head to Character Management, click Add Character to create one, then return to your launcher and click refresh.

**Launcher logs in fine, but I can't join my friend's server?**
Joining a multiplayer server with external auth requires that the server owner has also connected their server's authentication backend to this site. If the server only accepts official Mojang accounts or uses a different auth server, this site's credentials won't work there. Check with the server host about their supported login methods.

## Still not resolved?

If you have reviewed all the steps above and are still stuck, don't worry! Head over to [Ask for help](/manual/help) to gather your version details, steps to reproduce, and screenshots, then reach out to the site administration team for assistance.
help:
Running into a missing skin, launcher error, or unexpected behavior in the blocky world happens to every player now and then. Don't let it ruin your day—in most cases, sorting out one or two small config details will have you up and running in no time.

Before reaching out to administrators, take a minute or two to scan our [FAQ](/manual/faq). It covers the most common snags and their quick fixes, meaning you can often solve the problem right away without waiting for a reply.

## What information to provide

If the FAQ doesn't solve your issue, our administration team and community members are more than happy to help. But remember, we can't see your computer screen from afar—sending a vague message like "my skin is broken" or "it doesn't work" usually requires many rounds of back-and-forth questions to figure out what's going on.

To help us help you get back to playing as quickly as possible, sharing these key details in your request will often let us spot the issue immediately:

- **Where the issue occurs**: Did an error pop up on the website, did login fail in your launcher, or is the skin missing inside the game world?
- **What you were doing**: What step did you start from, what did you expect to happen, and what actually appeared on your screen?
- **The error details**: The exact text of any error popup, or a clear, uncropped screenshot of your screen.
- **Your environment**: Your Minecraft game version, launcher name and version (e.g., HMCL, Prism, PCL2), mod loader (Forge, Fabric), and skin mod versions.
- **Relevant links and names**: If a specific texture is involved, share its detail page link; if it involves a character, include your character name.
- **What you've already tried**: For example, "I restarted the game and cleared the mod cache, but the default skin still appears."

For example: *"I'm playing Minecraft 1.20.1 Forge with CustomSkinLoader. The 3D preview in Character Management looks great, but in singleplayer I still see the default Steve skin. I placed the ExtraList file into the instance folder, and the launcher log mentions a connection timeout..."* This kind of description lets administrators pinpoint the trouble in minutes.

## Contact the site administrator

Every skin server has dedicated staff members. You can reach administrators through the contact channels listed on the homepage, footer, announcements, or community chat groups. If you run into login authentication issues when joining a specific Minecraft server, check with that server's owner first to confirm their supported login methods.

If you spot plagiarized textures, inappropriate content, or abusive comments in the library, please use the built-in report button on the page. You can track moderation progress anytime on your [My Report](/reports) page.

## Share screenshots and logs

When sharing log files or screenshots, develop a smart security habit: blur or crop out sensitive personal data such as site passwords, email verification links, access tokens, and device codes to protect your privacy.

When providing debug logs, sharing the relevant error stack trace and timestamps is plenty—there's no need to paste thousands of lines of startup spam. And remember: legitimate administrators will never ask for your account password. Guard your personal credentials carefully, and never disable server security just to silence an error message.
advanced-search:
Every search box on the site understands a small search expression language. Typing keywords alone works as before, and combining keywords, fields and logic narrows the results in one go.

## Opening advanced search

The tune button next to a search box opens the advanced search panel. It lists the fields that page supports together with their meaning and an example; clicking an example appends it to the search box so you can keep adding conditions. You can also write the expression yourself.

A typo will not stop you: input that does not read as fields and conditions is searched as a plain keyword instead. To try it out, use the search box in the [Skin Library](/skinlib).

## Combining conditions

Adjacent words mean "all of them must match". You can also spell out the logic with OR, NOT and parentheses. The lines below are written the same way in every language:

```text
cape blue
cape OR cloak
cape -worn
(cape OR cloak) blue
"blue cape"
```

- `cape blue`: contains both words
- `cape OR cloak`: contains either word
- `cape -worn`: contains `cape` but not `worn`, which also reads as `NOT worn`
- `(cape OR cloak) blue`: parentheses decide how conditions group
- `"blue cape"`: everything inside the quotes matches as one phrase

## Restricting fields and comparing values

A colon after a field name searches that field only. For text fields the colon means "contains"; for lists, numbers and dates it means "equals". Use `=`, `!=`, `~`, `>`, `>=`, `<` or `<=` for a more precise comparison, such as `likes>100`, `kind=skin` or `uploader~ali`.

A range is written `start..end`, includes both ends, and either end may be omitted, for example `likes:10..100` or `created:..2024-06`.

## Writing dates

Time fields accept a specific date or a relative one:

- `2024`, `2024-06` and `2024-06-15` stand for a whole year, month or day
- `today` and `yesterday` stand for today and yesterday
- `7d`, `2w`, `3m` and `1y` stand for the last 7 days, 2 weeks, 3 months and 1 year

Comparisons read the way you would expect: `created>=2024-06-15` includes that day, while `created>2024-06-15` only takes what comes after it.

## Things to keep in mind

Search conditions combine with the other filters on the page (category, sorting, status and so on) instead of replacing them. Input that cannot be parsed, or that has more conditions than the site will expand, is searched as a plain keyword instead, so it never interrupts the search. Only input longer than 500 characters is rejected, and the search box applies the same limit.
